saying: Most commenters call the two-axis framework a workable starting point but not a complete risk determination, asking FDA to account for reversibility, error detectability, time to harm, traceability, autonomy or clinical agency, and patient vulnerability. Many add that human oversight and downstream safeguards should lower risk only with proof they work; several say "incorrect output" omits harms of omission.

disagreement.text: Commenters split on structure: some want the two axes kept as the primary heuristic with reversibility, safeguards, time pressure and traceability operationalized as auditable modifiers, while others want the framework expanded into additional axes or a fuller multi-dimensional set of risk factors.

sides.summary: Keep two axes; treat added factors as modifiers on the existing framework.
Expand to additional axes or a multi-dimensional risk representation.
